neighbours.label: the end of a counterfactual role-taking clause ('if I were her', 'if you were the manager', 'si j'étais vous'), where the speaker imagines being someone else, as against ordinary real conditionals and past-time clauses
fire: Frankly, if I were the manager, I would sell the striker in January.
Tell me honestly: if you were the judge, what sentence would you give?
My sister said that if she were the principal, she would ban phones.
Look, if I were in your shoes, I would take the job in Seattle.
So, if you were the captain of that ship, would you turn back?
Personally, if I were the mayor of this town, I'd fix the roads first.
Between us, if I were him, I would apologise before the wedding.
Answer quickly: if you were a teacher, which subject would you pick?
quiet: Frankly, if the manager sells the striker, the fans will be furious.
Tell me honestly: when you were in court, what sentence did they give?
My sister said that when she was at school, phones were banned.
Look, if the bus is late again, I will take the train to Seattle.
So, after the captain of that ship turned back, the storm passed.
Personally, if the roads are not fixed soon, I will write to the council.
Between us, when I saw him at the wedding, he looked tired.
Answer quickly: if the test starts at nine, which room is it in?

predictions: fire 0.4-1.0 on the comma or word right after 'if I/you were <role>'; real conditionals ('if it rains') and 'when I was' below 0.15
